title: MZ Pixel perfect rendering incorrectly in fullscreen

posts.author: Tri
posts.body:
I've had this long time issue of whenever I fullscreen my game with MZ and pixel-perfect image rendering (VisuMZ) the pixels of everything will look off and weird. Singular pixels will either be half it's size or too large.
The first image is of the character standing in the middle of the room
while fullscreened.
The second image is the same though
windowed instead.
I've also noticed when standing in certain areas of the screen or in smaller rooms the sprite will render correctly? In the last image of the darker room, the character is standing
on the far right
of my screen in a
smaller room
and looks relatively fine.
I'm purely using VisuMZ's core engine plugin to render pixel perfect although every other plugin that renders pixel perfect keeps this issue. Any help would be greatly appreciated. Additionally, I've also tried changing screen width and height to no avail, though I'm currently at the default of 816 x 624.

posts.author: Eliaquim
posts.body:
Hi there!
One of the things that can be causing this is a incompatible fullscreen resolution.
Let's say you have a 2560x1440 monitor.
Your game resolution is 816x624.
When you go fullscreen, the game's resolution will try to fit into your monitor resolution. It will calculate how far it can go:
Width → 2560/816 = 3,137254901960784
height → 1440/624 = 2,307692307692308
So your game height is being multiplied by
2,307692307692308
and your game width is being multiplied by
3,137254901960784
. It's impossivle to keep a pixel perfect while the game window is resizing like that.
That is why resolution matters. You either need to have a game resolution that can match the most common resolutions(16/9) or find a way to resize the screen only by integer numbers.
You can try using my EliMZ_ScreenManager for that. It has an option to scale the window only by integers. So your game resolution will scale width and height by the same integer number.
On the example above, using my plugin, it would let your game with that resolution:
816*2 =
1632
624*2 =
1248
Because he know if it go higher than that, it will have to fit into the fullscreen and scramble the aspect ratio.
